responseText: {"title":"The Shape of a Mouth","question":"When teeth appear in so many different constructions, what keeps an expression from settling into one feeling?","introduction":"Twenty-three heads, each built around an open mouth. Some bare teeth in tight rows, others spread them wide across a dark void; some surround them with spirals and zigzags, others with flat color or scribbled lines. Moving through the gallery, the same raw material — white marks against a dark gap — keeps shifting between a grin, a grimace, a shout, and something that refuses all three.","closing":"The tooth row reappears in every room, drawn differently each time. Whether any single construction resolves into an expression is a question the works leave open.","chapters":[{"title":"The Mouth as Anchor","introduction":"Four works where the mouth is the structural center of gravity — the feature everything else orbits rather than accompanies.","stops":[{"slot":"W007","whyHere":"A red-rimmed tooth row dominates the lower face; the circular form and radiating lines all press outward from that white-block mouth as their source.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W053","whyHere":"Three uneven eyes overhead, but the wide dark void between two tooth rows is the true anchor — the body mass and scribbled lines radiate from it.","transitionFromPrevious":"W007's mouth sits inside a circular boundary; here the mouth breaks free of any containing shape, becoming the widest opening in the frame."},{"slot":"W168","whyHere":"A jaw-like form fills the entire canvas; the tooth row is not a feature of a face but the face itself, with eye zones as secondary marks.","transitionFromPrevious":"W053 surrounds its mouth with a body; W168 removes that body almost entirely, leaving the jaw and tooth row as the whole composition."},{"slot":"W048","whyHere":"Two stacked jaw forms, one crowned by a spiral eye, double the mouth motif; the composition is built from nothing but jaw shapes layered vertically.","transitionFromPrevious":"W168 gives one jaw the whole canvas; W048 stacks two jaw forms on top of each other, making the doubling itself the subject."}]},{"title":"Teeth Inside a Decorated Field","introduction":"Works where the mouth competes with dense borders, zigzag lines, and ornamental marks — the tooth row present but surrounded by equal noise.","stops":[{"slot":"W044","whyHere":"A marquee-like border of repeating ovals and rectangles frames the bared mouth; the decoration and the teeth carry equal visual weight.","transitionFromPrevious":"W048's jaws push outward against a loose field; W044 locks its mouth inside a tight decorative border that holds it at the same pitch."},{"slot":"W069","whyHere":"A hot coral field and spiked crown compete with the white tooth row; the mouth is one loud element among several rather than the sole focus.","transitionFromPrevious":"W044's border is geometric and regular; W069 replaces it with organic zigzags and radiating spikes that press against the mouth from all sides."},{"slot":"W121","whyHere":"Zigzag teeth rows appear inside rectangular eye zones as well as the mouth, spreading the tooth motif across the whole face structure.","transitionFromPrevious":"W069's decoration stays outside the face; W121 folds the zigzag mark into the eye zones themselves, so teeth appear in multiple registers at once."},{"slot":"W157","whyHere":"Nested concentric loops surround both the mouth and the eye zones; the tooth row sits inside layered red and orange rings that echo the eye framing above.","transitionFromPrevious":"W121 uses zigzag lines throughout; W157 replaces the zigzag with concentric rectangular loops, giving the same density a more compressed, inward pull."},{"slot":"W287","whyHere":"Spiky crown forms above each rectangular eye zone and a countable tooth row below; the decorative and the dental are distributed evenly across the whole face.","transitionFromPrevious":"W157's loops press inward on a black ground; W287 opens onto a blue field where the same density of marks feels more exposed and frontal."}]},{"title":"Grounds That Change the Reading","introduction":"Six works where the background color — amber, coral, yellow, purple, teal, or bubble-covered yellow — actively alters how the mouth reads.","stops":[{"slot":"W059","whyHere":"A flat amber field holds the head steady while the red spiral eye and open bared teeth create competing focal points; the warm ground keeps neither from dominating.","transitionFromPrevious":"W287's blue field presses the face forward; W059's amber ground holds the head at a slight distance, making the open mouth feel less confrontational and more ambiguous."},{"slot":"W078","whyHere":"An open jaw and hollow sockets read as distress, but the acid-yellow ground and overlapping translucent circles push against that with something almost festive.","transitionFromPrevious":"W059's amber is warm but neutral; W078's yellow ground and bubble pattern create a direct visual argument with the skeletal jaw form above it."},{"slot":"W228","whyHere":"A flat bright blue field holds a face where heart and flower shapes stand in for eyes; the bared alternating teeth below sit in odd company with those tender eye forms.","transitionFromPrevious":"W078's ground fights its subject; W228's blue field is calm enough that the contrast between the flower-eye and the tooth row reads as a quieter, stranger tension."},{"slot":"W262","whyHere":"Saturated yellow pushes the central form forward; two red heart eye zones and a raw tooth row below create a compressed, contradictory surface.","transitionFromPrevious":"W228's blue holds the face at a distance; W262's yellow advances it, making the same heart-eye and tooth-row combination feel louder and more insistent."},{"slot":"W073","whyHere":"Dense black loops over ochre and teal washes build a rounded head; the red-edged mouth bares a tight, narrow tooth row rather than a wide-open jaw.","transitionFromPrevious":"W262's yellow field is flat and advancing; W073's layered ochre and teal washes give the ground depth, and the mouth closes slightly — teeth present but not gaping."},{"slot":"W277","whyHere":"A teal-green field surrounds a heavy circular form; warm reds and oranges inside contrast with the cool ground, and the spiked jaw below reads differently against that temperature shift.","transitionFromPrevious":"W073's ochre washes are warm throughout; W277 splits warm interior from cool exterior, so the jaw and tooth marks read as heat pressing against a cooler surround."}]},{"title":"Two Faces, One Field","introduction":"Works where a second face, eye, or mouth form shares the composition — the tooth row multiplied or placed in dialogue with another presence.","stops":[{"slot":"W115","whyHere":"Two face-like forms share a black field: a ringed eye on the left, an open-mouthed form with visible teeth on the right — neither merges with the other.","transitionFromPrevious":"W277's single circular form sits alone in its field; W115 places two distinct face-like structures side by side, making the gap between them as legible as either form."},{"slot":"W229","whyHere":"Two tooth-lined shapes appear within a single white-outlined oval, separated by a bold red-orange bar; the doubling reads as noise rather than a second voice.","transitionFromPrevious":"W115's two forms are spatially separate; W229 folds two tooth rows inside one outline, so the doubling is compressed and harder to resolve."},{"slot":"W259","whyHere":"A tilted head holds two yellow circular eyes and several rows of teeth; the multiplication of tooth rows makes a single expression impossible to isolate.","transitionFromPrevious":"W229's doubled teeth sit inside a flat purple field; W259 tilts the whole head and adds warm color bands, so the crowded tooth rows feel kinetic rather than static."},{"slot":"W253","whyHere":"A circular form under pressure from lines pulling outward in every direction; the open lower section packed with white verticals reads as a shout caught mid-release.","transitionFromPrevious":"W259's tilted head is dense but contained; W253 breaks the containing form open, with lines escaping outward and the tooth-like verticals exposed inside a dark cavity."}]},{"title":"Surface Pressure and the Unresolved Face","introduction":"Five works where layered marks, scribble lines, and color patches build so much surface pressure that the mouth expression becomes the last thing to settle.","stops":[{"slot":"W015","whyHere":"A grinning yellow disc crossed by bars edged with teeth; the smile sits below crossed marks, making the grin and the threat coexist on the same surface.","transitionFromPrevious":"W253's form is circular and under outward pressure; W015 is also a disc, but the pressure comes from crossed bars and a heavy red field pressing inward from below."},{"slot":"W182","whyHere":"A swollen olive-green face pushes against the frame; crossed scribbles in acid yellow and cyan sit over the bulk without softening it, and the bared teeth read as confrontational.","transitionFromPrevious":"W015's disc floats in its field; W182's face fills the frame completely, removing any breathing room between the bared teeth and the viewer."},{"slot":"W232","whyHere":"Two mismatched eyes — one gridded, one crossed out — give the face an off-balance stare; drips from above and the open-toothed mouth below pull the eye in opposite directions.","transitionFromPrevious":"W182's surface is dense but symmetrical; W232 introduces deliberate asymmetry between the two eye zones, so the face reads as unstable rather than merely loud."},{"slot":"W268","whyHere":"Dark layered color pools inside the form while bright scattered lines fly outward; the bared tooth row and goggle shapes read as raw alarm against the black field.","transitionFromPrevious":"W232's gray ground gives the face some neutral space; W268's black field removes it entirely, making the contrast between the dark core and the escaping bright lines feel abrupt."},{"slot":"W287","whyHere":"Already seen in Chapter Two, but here its role shifts: the blue field and countable tooth row now read as the most legible, least pressured surface in this final sequence — a point of relative clarity before the gallery ends.","transitionFromPrevious":"W268's interior is dark and compressed; W287's blue field and clean white outlines open the surface back up, making the same tooth row feel exposed rather than buried."}]}]}
